status.comment: Owner request of 2026-09-16: finish Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and Qwen Code, including pause and background wake. Extends the accepted local product boundary; implementation and live evidence must be recorded separately.

p.scope: The same project lifecycle and addressed background delivery are implemented for all four registered provider families. Owned structured coordinators and owned interactive managed workers retain distinct execution mechanisms. Configured native integrations may report their actual supported session controls. Observing an arbitrary external session does not confer ownership of its desktop window or terminal.

p.pause: Pause commits the project/context dispatch fence before requesting provider control. An already idle owned session can settle immediately. Active work is interrupted using a verified provider mechanism, and the project remains pausing until all relevant owned work is observed settled. An interruption request alone is not settlement. The same conversation, task lineage, questions, answers and queued inputs remain retained. Pause does not promise freezing and resuming a remote model computation at an identical token.

p.continuation: Explicit Continue re-enables dispatch for the exact project/context and resumes its known provider conversation where process recreation is necessary. It preserves pinned model/effort and trusted agent bindings and does not resend the full coordinator bootstrap. Stored source/plan changes remain available for reconciliation before new mutations. Stop is distinct from Pause; neither state can be cleared by a background event. A lost session requires an explicit recovery state rather than a silent new expensive coordinator.

p.wake-queue: An actionable addressed event creates a durable wake notice on the shared server. Notices retain project/context, intended actor, source event, question/answer version or child result identity, and delivery state. The server submits notice input through a verified provider route only when the exact owned session is ready and automation owns control. Busy sessions retain notices until an observed safe point; paused/stopped projects retain them until Continue. No model polling loop implements waiting. Multiple events may be coalesced without dropping their identities.

p.delivery: Persistence, claimed dispatch, host acceptance, observed reply and broker acknowledgement are separate facts. Retries preserve stable identities and fence process/session/control epochs. Uncertain transport after a possible side effect is retained for reconciliation instead of blind duplicate submission. A native turn identifier is stored only when the provider supplied it; otherwise an explicit transport correlation links the accepted message and observed response. Parent notification of a child result or reply does not claim that the child consumed an answer.

p.managed-control: Managed workers remain real interactive CLI/TUI processes in owned pseudoterminals. Verified structured sidebands, provider server APIs or authenticated configured hooks may observe readiness and support control. Screen colors, prompt-looking text, quiet output and guessed delays are not authoritative idle or permission state. Human input ownership fences automated wake. A wake never answers a native permission prompt, grants plan authority or transfers terminal control. Interrupt and resume preserve the declared project and attempt.

p.events: User chat, rich question answers and amendments, meaningful cancellation notices and child-result availability use the same scoped dispatch discipline. Passive notes remain passive; deferred instructions stay attached until their declared work boundary. New specifications may signal changed source state without forcing an interruption of the current turn. Reconnect and restart preserve queued notices, their prior delivery observations and paused state.

p.shared-clients: Wayfinder owns lifecycle, queues and capability observations for every Lens client. Quick Lens displays requested pause, pausing, paused, continuation, queued wake and delivery failure distinctly. Controls are based on verified installed capabilities and current ownership. Opening another client does not create another wake dispatcher or duplicate a model turn.

p.acceptance: Acceptance uses bounded actual checks for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and Qwen Code with explicitly selected inexpensive models, plus deterministic integration checks for project isolation, busy-to-idle delivery, pause retention, Continue, duplicate events, uncertain send and human terminal control. At least one actual idle agent must receive a late answer without having a blocking inbox wait in flight. Active pause is checked through provider settlement, and continuation reuses its conversation. Actual provider credentials, model availability or version limits are reported precisely; a fake process or a capability flag is not evidence of a real provider primitive. This is a support check, not a comparative model-quality benchmark.
